page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a burstable compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor configured with 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs with hyper-threading enabled. System memory consists of 96 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of compute-oriented hardware profiles. Processor caching includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache array. Advanced hardware features include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) alongside AVX-512, VAES, and SHA extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7i-flex.12xlarge displays strong capabilities across memory bandwidth and specialized instruction tests. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 222.1 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 72.85 GB/sec and Redis SET operations hit 62.18 million operations per second. Multi-threaded processing scores high in software compilation with Clang and bzip3 decompression, alongside solid Passmark CPU encryption results. In CPU-based machine learning benchmarks, the system achieves top-tier inference speeds of 353.0 tokens per second for small 135M parameter LLM text generation, while maintaining strong performance for 7B parameter model prompt processing.

The instance relies on network-attached storage, as no local NVMe drives are included in the baseline hardware configuration. External network connectivity is provided via a 9 Gbps baseline interface without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because the CPU allocation utilizes a burstable model rather than dedicated fixed cores, resource efficiency is high for workloads with variable utilization profiles, delivering favorable cost-per-compute dynamics compared to fully provisioned instances. Tradeoffs include potential performance variance during sustained peak load periods if CPU credits deplete.

Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is targeted at workloads requiring high multi-threaded compute density and modern CPU instruction extensions without dedicated local disks. Prime application domains include CI/CD software compilation pipelines, web application serving, Redis caching nodes, database operations, and lightweight CPU-based AI inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized, burstable virtual server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor, it delivers 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores along with 105 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes 96 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio optimized for compute-heavy processing. Built-in hardware accelerators support Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, driving strong benchmark results in software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference. It provides a 9 Gbps baseline network interface without bundled local NVMe storage. Because the instance uses a burstable CPU allocation model, it offers a cost-effective alternative to fixed-performance compute nodes for variable workloads. Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is suitable for batch processing, web serving, software build pipelines, and machine learning inference tasks.
